sections.title: Distance of Point & Parallel Lines
sections.content: Perpendicular distance from (x1,y1) to ax+by+c=0 is d = |ax1+by1+c| / √(a²+b²). Distance between parallel lines ax+by+c1=0 and ax+by+c2=0 is d = |c1-c2| / √(a²+b²).

sections.title: Foot of Perpendicular & Image
sections.content: For a point (x1,y1) and line ax+by+c=0, the foot (x,y) is given by: (x-x1)/a = (y-y1)/b = -(ax1+by1+c)/(a²+b²). For the image, multiply the RHS by 2.

sections.title: Family of Lines
sections.content: The equation of any line passing through the intersection of two lines L1=0 and L2=0 is L1 + λL2 = 0, where λ is a parameter found using an additional given condition.

sections.title: Tangent to a Circle
sections.content: Point form (at x1,y1): T = xx1 + yy1 + g(x+x1) + f(y+y1) + c = 0. Slope form (for x²+y²=a²): y = mx ± a√(1+m²). Condition of tangency: perpendicular distance from center = radius.

sections.title: Director Circle and Chord of Contact
sections.content: Director circle is the locus of intersection of perpendicular tangents. For x²+y²=a², it is x²+y²=2a². Chord of contact of tangents drawn from external point (x1,y1) is exactly T = 0.

sections.title: Length of Tangent & Power of Point
sections.content: The length of a tangent from an external point (x1,y1) to circle S=0 is √S1. The Power of a Point is exactly S1.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
1) Confusing T=0 for tangent vs. chord of contact. (T=0 is tangent if point is ON the circle, chord of contact if OUTSIDE).
2) Forgetting to make x/y coefficients identical before applying distance between parallel lines formula.
3) Missing the ± sign in slope form of tangents (there are two parallel tangents for a given slope).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 handles distances, reflections (images), and lines interacting with circles (tangents, normal, chord of contact). The 'T' notation becomes your strongest algebraic tool here.

tricks.title: Image of Origin Shortcut
tricks.explanation: The image of (0,0) in the line ax+by+c=0 is simply (-2ac/(a²+b²), -2bc/(a²+b²)).

tricks.title: T = 0 Ambiguity Resolution
tricks.explanation: Write T=0. If the point (x1,y1) satisfies S=0, it's a Tangent. If S>0, it's the Chord of Contact. If S<0, it's the Polar line.
tricks.example: For x²+y²=4 and point (3,0), T=0 is 3x=4. Since 3²+0² > 4, it is a chord of contact.

tricks.title: Normal always passes through Center
tricks.explanation: To find the normal to a circle at a point, simply write the equation of the line joining that point and the center of the circle.
tricks.example: Normal to x²+y²=4 at (2,0) joins (2,0) and (0,0), which is the X-axis (y=0).

tricks.title: Chord with Given Middle Point
tricks.explanation: If (x1, y1) is the midpoint of a chord of circle S=0, the equation of the chord is T = S1.

tricks.title: Concurrency of 3 Lines Check
tricks.explanation: Three lines a1x+b1y+c1=0, a2x+b2y+c2=0, a3x+b3y+c3=0 are concurrent if the 3x3 determinant of their coefficients is zero.

tricks.title: Tangent Condition Shortcut
tricks.explanation: A line y = mx + c touches x² + y² = r² if c² = r²(1+m²).
tricks.example: y=x+c touches x²+y²=2 if c² = 2(1+1) = 4, so c = ±2.
